usdRate.sourceName: Banco Central de Cuba, official exchange rate, Segment III (households and non-state businesses)
usdRate.note: CUP 768.00 per US dollar for 31 October 2026 in Segment III, the rate used for household currency exchange; Segment I (state) is fixed at 24 and Segment II at 120. The Segment III rate was 411 in January 2026.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: ONEI (Oficina Nacional de Estadística e Información) CPI, September 2026, as reported by Directorio Cubano (secondary source)
inflation_cpi.note: Official year-on-year CPI inflation 28.44% in September 2026 (25.19% in August). ONEI's own site could not be reached (certificate error). Independent estimates put real inflation far higher.

inflation_projection.sourceName: ONEI CPI 28.4% in September 2026; official inflation about 25-40% a year since the 2021 currency reform; no inflation target
inflation_projection.note: With no credible inflation target and official inflation above 25% for most years since 2021, planning uses 25% a year.

policy_rate.note: The Banco Central de Cuba sets bank interest rates administratively and its monetary policy dashboard shows no published reference rate.

savings_account_rate.note: Deposit rates are set by the Banco Central de Cuba for state banks and are not published on its site; only bank pages show them.

fdr_3m_rate.note: Deposit rates are set by the Banco Central de Cuba for state banks and are not published on its site; only bank pages show them.

fdr_1y_rate.note: Deposit rates are set by the Banco Central de Cuba for state banks and are not published on its site; only bank pages show them.

dps_rate.note: No monthly recurring deposit product with a published rate was found.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: No published average deposit rate; the World Bank has no deposit-rate series for Cuba.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: No government savings certificate or retail bond is sold to individuals; government bonds are placed with state banks.

tbill_91d_rate.note: No treasury bills are sold to the public and no yield is published.

tbond_5y_rate.note: Government bonds are placed with state banks only; no market yield is published.

tbond_10y_rate.note: Government bonds are placed with state banks only; no market yield is published.

tax_bank_interest.note: No official or tax-guide source on taxation of personal bank interest under the Tax System Law (Ley 113) could be read.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No government savings certificate exists for individuals.

deposit_insurance_limit.note: No deposit insurance scheme or published cover limit was found; banks are state-owned.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: No published legal cap or typical rate for credit card balances was found.

equity_return_low.sourceName: No stock exchange in Cuba; Segment III official rate rose from 411 to 768 pesos per US dollar in 2026 (BCC)
equity_return_low.note: There is no local stock market and no legal way for most residents to buy a global index fund; low case kept just under the assumed safe rate.

equity_return_base.sourceName: No local market; capped at the assumed safe rate (3%) plus 4 points
equity_return_base.note: A global index in peso terms would track the peso's fall, but equity is not available to residents, so the base case is capped at 4 points over the assumed safe rate.

equity_return_high.sourceName: Global equity record; peso depreciation (BCC Segment III rate)
equity_return_high.note: High case for a resident with access to foreign assets.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Gold USD 3,876/oz on 30 Oct 2026 (Trading Economics); peso depreciation
gold_return_low.note: Low case: dollar gold flat while the peso keeps losing value more slowly than in 2026.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold USD trend plus peso depreciation: BCC Segment III rate 411 (Jan 2026) to 768 (Oct 2026) pesos per dollar
gold_return_base.note: Base case: gold in pesos rises roughly with the peso's depreciation, assumed at about 20% a year.

gold_return_high.sourceName: Peso lost almost half its official Segment III value in 2026 (BCC)
gold_return_high.note: High case: the peso keeps falling as fast as in 2026.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: BCC sets deposit rates administratively; not published on its site
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: an ordinary peso savings account, which pays very little.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: BCC sets deposit rates administratively; not published on its site
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: fixed-term peso deposits at state banks, assumed to pay low single-digit rates far below inflation.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: BCC sets deposit rates administratively; not published on its site
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: the longest fixed-term peso deposits.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: The insurance supervisor (Superintendencia de Seguros, Ministry of Finance and Prices) publishes no claim settlement statistics.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Life insurance is sold by state insurers, but no regulator or non-company source of term premiums by age was found.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Hospital care for residents is free in the public national health system; there are no private hospitals for residents and no published cost.

health_premium_table.note: No private health insurance market for residents was found.

oop_health_share.note: Out-of-pocket spending was 16.6% of current health expenditure in 2023 (latest available; older than 2025).

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: ONEI CPI 28.4% (September 2026); public care is free but medicines are scarce and bought informally
goal_inflation_health.note: No medical CPI was found; planning uses the general inflation assumption of 25%.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: ONEI CPI 28.4% (September 2026); public education is free
goal_inflation_education.note: No education CPI was found; planning uses the general inflation assumption of 25%.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_table_remaining.note: Remaining years derived from the 'life expectancy by current age' table for 2026 (UN WPP).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 25.1 in 2025 (World Bank), 48.3 in 2040 and 62.0 in 2065 (UN WPP).

retirement_age_default.sourceName: US SSA, Social Security Programs Throughout the World: The Americas, 2019, Cuba
retirement_age_default.note: Social Security Law 105 of 2008: old-age pension at 65 for men and 60 for women with 30 years of work (partial pension with 20-29 years). Source is from 2019, older than 2025; no later change was found.

retirement_age_government.sourceName: US SSA, Social Security Programs Throughout the World: The Americas, 2019, Cuba
retirement_age_government.note: The same social insurance rules cover public-sector employees: 65 for men, 60 for women. Source is from 2019, older than 2025.

retirement_return_low.sourceName: BCC sets deposit rates administratively; not published
retirement_return_low.note: Low case: savings account in pesos.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: BCC sets deposit rates administratively; not published
retirement_return_base.note: Base case: fixed-term peso deposits, assumed low single digits and no higher than the safe rate.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: BCC sets deposit rates administratively; not published
retirement_return_high.note: High case: longest fixed-term peso deposits.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: Peso deposits only; no local stock or bond market for individuals
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case: residents can mostly hold only peso deposits.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: Peso deposits; equity assumption capped at safe rate plus 4 points
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case for a mix weighted to peso deposits.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case for someone with some access to real or foreign assets.

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Means-tested social assistance pays older people who cannot work and have no family support, but the amount is set case by case and no current figure was found.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.sourceName: US SSA, Social Security Programs Throughout the World: The Americas, 2019, Cuba
old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Social assistance old-age benefit: men 65, women 60 with fewer than 20 years of work, unable to work and with no family members to support them. Source is from 2019, older than 2025.

gratuity_rule.note: No statutory gratuity or end-of-service payment for employees was found in the sources read.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: US SSA, Social Security Programs Throughout the World: The Americas, 2019, Cuba
public_pension_scheme.note: State social insurance (Law 105 of 2008) covers employees: pension at 65 (men) or 60 (women) with 30 years of work, 60% of best 5 of the last 15 years' average earnings; benefits are adjusted by government decree, not automatically for inflation. Source is from 2019.

fdr_3m.note: Offered by state savings banks; rates are not published by the central bank.

fdr_1y.note: Offered by state savings banks; rates are not published by the central bank.

dps.note: No monthly recurring deposit product was confirmed.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: Government bonds are placed with state banks, not sold to individuals.

equity_fund.note: Cuba has no stock exchange and no retail investment funds.

gold.note: No legal retail market for investment gold bars or coins was found.

insuranceRegulator.name: Superintendencia de Seguros, Ministerio de Finanzas y Precios

insuranceComplaints.name: Ministerio de Finanzas y Precios, citizen complaints (Superintendencia de Seguros)

pensionScheme.name: Seguridad social (Ley 105), Ministerio de Trabajo y Seguridad Social

oldAgeAllowance.name: Asistencia social, Ministerio de Trabajo y Seguridad Social
oldAgeAllowance.note: Means-tested social assistance, not a universal pension.

publicHealthCover.name: Sistema Nacional de Salud, Ministerio de Salud Pública (MINSAP)

statistics.name: Oficina Nacional de Estadística e Información (ONEI)
